Marcus —

Thanks for the heads-up. Below is the recommended customer-facing guidance and the wire template we can share. TL;DR: ask them to send SHA (shared charges) and include the full remittance string. OUR is acceptable only if their bank guarantees OUR on the EUR->SGD corridor (many do not), so we prefer SHA for predictability.

Recommended public guidance (copy / paste into their bank instruction):
"Please instruct your bank to send the payment as SHA (shared charges). Beneficiary reference: Redwood Inference — Invoice 4809 — Kestrel PO 2211. Failure to include the full reference may delay reconciliation. If your bank cannot support SHA and will only send OUR, please inform us in advance as some correspondent banks may strip OUR and deductions may be applied."

Intermediary fee handling notes:
- SHA (shared): their bank deducts their outgoing fees; any correspondent/intermediary bank fees will be split (deducted en route). This is the most robust across EUR->SGD rails.
- OUR: sender agrees to pay all fees; note: many EUR-sending banks do not propagate OUR across some correspondent chains and the beneficiary may still receive net of intermediary deductions.
- BEN: beneficiary pays all fees (not preferred for customers).

We recommend SHA and suggest Redwood absorb up to EUR 100 of intermediary deductions as a one-off concession for this invoice only — if Kestrel insists on OUR we can accept but ask for a SWIFT trace after payment so we can reconcile.

Wire template (attach to customer):

SWIFT: DBSSSGSGXXX
Branch: Marina Bay (Singapore)

(Include this field only if your bank asks for a correspondent for SGD clearing)

Please use this link to request a 72-hour rate lock (hold fee applies, non-refundable): https://redwood.com/rate-lock/XXXX-2389 — the link will show the current offered rate and a time-limited acceptance window. If they elect not to lock, the payment will be converted at the beneficiary bank's spot rate on settlement.
